purpose: Source-specific, paraphrased evidence index. Raw primary text and retrieval responses remain in the immutable research archive. This index is evidence for its literal database/table projections, not a substitute primary quotation.

PMID:25175347.title: Mutations in APOPT1, encoding a mitochondrial protein, cause cavitating leukoencephalopathy with cytochrome c oxidase deficiency.
PMID:25175347.finding: Human variants cause complex IV deficiency; M14-derived COA8 partly rescues the patient-cell defect and oxidative stress increases the mature protein.
PMID:25175347.access_and_scope: Selected full Results and Discussion were read, including construct starts, import, patient complementation, knockdown and negative apoptosis observations. Its mitochondrial localization does not independently establish inner-membrane sidedness.

PMID:28514442.title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
PMID:28514442.finding: Human COA8 bait co-purifies with CLUH in BioPlex; the assay supports association, without direct affinity or a functional mechanism.
PMID:28514442.access_and_scope: Selected full AP-MS Results and Methods and the exact 42-field COA8–CLUH record were read. Pipeline validation is not asserted for the individual pair.

PMID:30552096.title: APOPT1/COA8 assists COX assembly and is oppositely regulated by UPS and ROS.
PMID:30552096.finding: Human complementation and pulse-chase experiments connect COA8 to complex IV assembly and subunit stability; stress-dependent accumulation and matrix-side association are experimentally supported.
PMID:30552096.access_and_scope: Selected full human and mouse Results and Methods were read. Results paragraph 71 supports a matrix-facing C terminus, whereas Discussion paragraph 114 says IMS-facing; the experimental Results guide localization. Paper APOPT1-201/203 constructs are not automatically equated to both current UniProt products.

PMID:33961781.title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
PMID:33961781.finding: BioPlex extends human co-complex evidence. The CLUH-specific original assertion remains separate from the COX10 association.
PMID:33961781.access_and_scope: The protected main cache is limited; the separately archived genuine normal full variant supplied selected AP-MS Results and Methods. Exact COA8–CLUH and COX10–COA8 records were inspected, with their distinct bait/prey assignments.

PMID:34800366.title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
PMID:34800366.finding: MitoCoP provides positive mitochondrial proteomic detection of COA8.
PMID:34800366.access_and_scope: Selected full Methods and original Table S1 were read. Q96IL0/APOPT1 is explicit in both the all-proteins and MitoCoP sheets; this is a gene/protein-group detection, not proof of an isoform or membrane leaflet.

PMID:16782708.title: Apop-1, a novel protein inducing cyclophilin D-dependent but Bax/Bak-related channel-independent apoptosis.
PMID:16782708.finding: Mouse apoptogenic expression, cytochrome c release, caspase activation, cyclophilin-D controls and antisense suppression support a conditional apoptosis role.
PMID:16782708.access_and_scope: The normal cache is abstract-only; authentic author-uploaded article text supplied selected Methods, Results and Discussion. Mouse Apop-1 is 194 residues and its alternative Apop-2 differs at the C terminus. Human host cells do not turn the mouse construct into direct human protein evidence.

PMID:18977203.title: Akt activation prevents Apop-1-induced death of cells.
PMID:18977203.finding: IGF-1 protects against Apop-1-induced death in the studied vascular smooth-muscle context via PI3K/Akt signaling.
PMID:18977203.access_and_scope: The complete authentic abstract was read; no full-paper or construct-sequence claim is made.

PMID:31555154.title: Knockdown of APOPT1/COA8 Causes Cytochrome c Oxidase Deficiency, Neuromuscular Impairment, and Reduced Resistance to Oxidative Stress in Drosophila melanogaster.
PMID:31555154.finding: The reviewed fly ortholog localizes to mitochondria and its depletion impairs complex IV-related phenotypes.
PMID:31555154.access_and_scope: Selected full fly Methods, localization Results and Figure 1 legend were read. Predicted membrane topology is distinguished from actual mitochondrial GFP/MitoTracker colocalization.

PMID:29577824.title: Cavitating Leukoencephalopathy With Posterior Predominance Caused by a Deletion in the APOPT1 Gene in an Indian Boy.
PMID:29577824.finding: Additional human APOPT1 variants support the cavitating-leukoencephalopathy disease context.

DOI:10.1101/2024.04.02.587738.title: COA8 is a COX10-binding protein involved in the early biogenesis of cytochrome c oxidase
DOI:10.1101/2024.04.02.587738.finding: Human COA8 associates with COX10. A W174A variant retains binding and restores COX10 abundance but fails to restore heme A and complex IV, separating association from functional rescue.
DOI:10.1101/2024.04.02.587738.access_and_scope: Unreviewed 2024 preprint, version 2. Official bioRxiv and Crossref records were checked; the normal DOI cache is abstract-only after provider failures. A genuine repository PDF supplied actual selected Results and Methods. Human HA-SILAC and GFP co-IP demonstrate association; heme pool measurements and predicted interfaces do not constitute purified COX10 catalytic-rate or COA8 catalytic assays.

binding.scope: Two original CLUH pair assertions are retained separately. A third COX10-bait association record corroborates a different pair and does not retarget either original source. AP-MS shows co-association; direct binary affinity and universal native localization are not inferred.

definition.text: The inner, i.e. lumen-facing, lipid bilayer of the mitochondrial envelope. It is highly folded to form cristae.
A semiautonomous, self replicating organelle that occurs in varying numbers, shapes, and sizes in the cytoplasm of virtually all eukaryotic cells. It is notably the site of tissue respiration.

GO:0033617.name: mitochondrial respiratory chain complex IV assembly

definition.text: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form respiratory chain complex IV (also known as cytochrome c oxidase) in the mitochondrial inner membrane.
Binding to a protein or a protein-containing complex to assist the protein folding process, driven by ATP hydrolysis.

GO:0099617.name: matrix side of mitochondrial inner membrane

definition.text: The leaflet of a mitochondrial inner membrane that faces the matrix, including any protein embedded in, attached to, or peripherally associated with it.

A programmed cell death process which begins when a cell receives an internal (e.g. DNA damage) or external signal (e.g. an extracellular death ligand), and proceeds through a series of biochemical events (signaling pathway phase) which trigger an execution phase. The execution phase is the last step of an apoptotic process, and is typically characterized by rounding-up of the cell, retraction of pseudopodes, reduction of cellular volume (pyknosis), chromatin condensation, nuclear fragmentation (karyorrhexis), plasma membrane blebbing and fragmentation of the cell into apoptotic bodies. When the execution phase is completed, the cell has died.

GO:0006919.name: obsolete activation of cysteine-type endopeptidase activity involved in apoptotic process

definition.text: OBSOLETE. Any process that initiates the activity of the inactive enzyme cysteine-type endopeptidase in the context of an apoptotic process.

The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form respiratory chain complex IV (also known as cytochrome c oxidase), the terminal member of the respiratory chain of the mitochondrion and some aerobic bacteria. Cytochrome c oxidases are multi-subunit enzymes containing from 13 subunits in the mammalian mitochondrial form to 3-4 subunits in the bacterial forms.
Any process involved in maintaining the structure and integrity of a protein and preventing it from degradation or aggregation.

Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a reactive oxygen species stimulus. Reactive oxygen species include singlet oxygen, superoxide, and oxygen free radicals.

The series of molecular signals in which an intracellular signal is conveyed to trigger the apoptotic death of a cell. The pathway starts with reception of an intracellular signal (e.g. DNA damage, endoplasmic reticulum stress, oxidative stress etc.), and ends when the execution phase of apoptosis is triggered. The intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway is crucially regulated by permeabilization of the mitochondrial outer membrane (MOMP).
A structural molecule activity of a protein-containing complex component that serves to hold the complex together. Protein complex scaffolds are integral members of complexes.
Binding to an enzyme, a protein with catalytic activity.

propagation_scope: The PTN query did not reconstruct ancestral placement. Current positive human/mouse experimental records and fly primary microscopy support mitochondrial residence; target self-inclusion is legitimate. The human matrix-side replacement is independent target evidence, not a claim of universal conserved sidedness.
ontology_scope: GO:0099617 includes peripherally associated proteins and is part of the inner membrane; no integral-membrane inference. GO:0019899 is a protein-binding child, so no redundant NEW binding row is added. GO:0140777 requires exclusion of a dissociation factor, not demonstrated here. GO:0110078 is a cellular component and is excluded as an activity. No new process is proposed.

mitocop_target.scope: Positive protein-group mitochondrial detection; no isoform-discriminating or membrane-sidedness claim. The historical apoptosis description in the workbook is annotation metadata, not a new apoptosis experiment.
